claim: Of subject–auxiliary inversion in the protasis (as in [47i] Had I had any inkling of this, I would have acted differently), p. 753 says “It is restricted to remote conditionals”, and p. 754 continues “except that the special conditional should allows inversion in both open and remote constructions”.
evidence_summary: Ch. 11 p. 970 [55iii] is an open conditional with inversion and no status mark: Dare a woman have a child, she’s putting her job at risk. The commentary says “Example [iii] is unusual in that we have here an open conditional: these inverted conditional adjuncts normally occur in remote conditionals”. Page 753 cites Ch. 11, §4.7 two sentences earlier.
finding: Medium confidence: Ch. 8 states as categorical what Ch. 11 states as the norm, and Ch. 11 gives an open example. Ch. 11 p. 970 calls the example “unusual”, which supports Ch. 8 only if p. 753 is read as hedged; adding normally would reconcile the two.
proposed_wording: It is normally restricted to remote conditionals
inference: Is subject–auxiliary inversion in a conditional protasis restricted to remote conditionals?

evidence.passage: §14.2.2, p. 753. “It is restricted to remote conditionals”
evidence.example: Ch. 11 p. 970 [55iii], Dare a woman have a child, she’s putting her job at risk.
evidence.establishes: The book’s own example of an open inverted conditional, with a hedged statement of the norm.
